findings.title: Exhausted-codes cleanup treats a federated credential as a locally stored one
findings.description:
The authenticator now resolves the credential through `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential`, which prefers the user-storage credential. The follow-up logic still assumes a locally stored credential.

- **Removal never reaches the user storage.** When `allCodesUsed()` is true, line 86 calls `removeStoredCredentialById(...)`. That routes to `getStoreForUser(user)` (`UserCredentialManager.java:114-117`), which is the Keycloak DB store, so the exhausted federated credential stays in place.
- **The ID may be null.** `createFromCredentialModel` copies the ID from the provider's model. The test provider builds its model with `createFromValues`, which sets no ID (`RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.java:58-85`). A null ID would reach `em.find(FederatedUserCredentialEntity.class, id, ...)` at `JpaUserFederatedStorageProvider.java:602`, which per the JPA contract rejects a null key. I did not execute this path.

The exhaustion path needs a federated branch, for example `disableCredentialType` as `CredentialDeleteHelper.java:68` does, or a guard so the stored-credential removal only runs for stored credentials.

findings.title: Login form throws if the user storage accepts recovery codes but does not expose them via getCredentials
findings.description:
`CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential` (`CredentialHelper.java:125-130`) skips local creation whenever the user storage's `updateCredential` returns true. Rendering the input form then depends on the provider also returning the credential from `getCredentials`, whose default is `Stream.empty()` (`CredentialInputUpdater.java:50-52`).

- **Missing credential.** A provider that implements update, `isConfiguredFor` and `isValid` but not `getCredentials` leaves `getCredential` empty. `credentialModelOpt.get()` at line 19 then throws `NoSuchElementException` from `FreeMarkerLoginFormsProvider.java:272`.
- **Format requirement.** The returned model must carry `credentialData` and `secretData` in Keycloak's internal JSON format, or `createFromCredentialModel` fails.
- **Before this change** the required action always created the local credential, so the bean always found one.

The `Optional` is assigned and immediately unwrapped, so it adds no safety. Handle the empty case explicitly and document the provider contract on `getCredential` and `createRecoveryCodesCredential`.

findings.title: New test covers only the happy path, and the test provider cannot detect one-time-use regressions
Test helpers copied verbatim from RecoveryAuthnCodesAuthenticatorTest
findings.description: `configureBrowserFlowWithRecoveryAuthnCodes` duplicates `RecoveryAuthnCodesAuthenticatorTest.java:123-143`, and `enterRecoveryCodes` (lines 476-483) duplicates `RecoveryAuthnCodesAuthenticatorTest.java:299-306`. The copy keeps the `"delayed-suthenticator-config"` typo and a `delay` parameter that is only ever 0 here. `enterRecoveryCodes` also takes `enterRecoveryAuthnCodePage` and `driver` as parameters that shadow the fields of the same name. Extract both into a shared helper next to `FlowUtil` or the page object.

findings.title: "Backwards compatibility 4.8.3" provider now depends on newer APIs and changes existing OTP behaviour
Null-safety and error handling in the test provider are inconsistent with the surrounding methods
findings.description:
- `getCredentials` dereferences `myUser` without a null check, while `getDisableableCredentialTypesStream` (line 259), `isConfiguredFor` (line 271) and `isValid` (line 286) all guard it.
- The `IOException` at lines 243-245 is logged without the exception or the username, and the credential is silently dropped.
- `credentialType.equals(RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE)` at lines 114 and 275 is null-unsafe and reversed relative to the constant-first style on line 112.
- Raw `List` and `List.class` at lines 238, 332 and 334 produce unchecked warnings.
- `disableCredentialType` and `getDisableableCredentialTypesStream` were not extended, so a recovery-codes credential in this provider can never be removed.

findings.title: Plaintext codes are handed to the user storage under an undocumented format
findings.description: `createRecoveryCodesCredential` passes the raw codes as a JSON array in the `challengeResponse` of a `UserCredentialModel`. This is necessary for the provider to hash and store them, but the one-line Javadoc does not say so. It also omits that `generatedCodes` must match the codes inside `credentialModel`, and that the provider must hash them and serve them back from `getCredentials`. The test provider stores the plaintext JSON in `credentialData` (line 197), which is a poor example for implementers.

findings.title: Hard-coded provider ID and minor inconsistencies in createRecoveryCodesCredential
findings.description:
- The literal `"keycloak-recovery-authn-codes"` duplicates `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProviderFactory.PROVIDER_ID` (line 11 of that file). The module boundary prevents a direct reference, and it mirrors `"keycloak-otp"` on line 93, but a rename will not be caught by the compiler.
- The provider is resolved as a raw `CredentialProvider` before it is known to be needed.
- `throw new RuntimeException(e)` at line 121 has no message.
- `RecoveryAuthnCodesAction.java:28` uses a static import, whereas the existing call style is qualified (`CredentialHelper.createOTPCredential` at `UpdateTotp.java:119`).

findings.title: Cosmetic issues and unrelated reformatting
findings.description:
- The Javadoc reads "a optional credential model", and the method name `getCredential` does not convey the federated-first lookup order. - Double spaces appear at `CredentialHelper.java:119`, and at `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java:244` and `:341`. - The diff carries unrelated whitespace churn: the `getConfigurableAuthenticatorFactory` re-indent, the `

` Javadoc edit, and the `TypeReference<>() {\n }` reformat at `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorageTest.java:467-468`. - `getCredential` calls the user storage on every form render and every submit, which may be a remote round trip for real providers.

findings.title: Local-storage behaviour is preserved for non-federated users
findings.description:
- **Lookup.** For non-federated users `getFederatedCredentialsStream()` returns `Stream.empty()` (`UserCredentialManager.java:130-146`), so `getCredential` falls through to the same stored-credential lookup as before.
- **Creation.** No built-in credential provider implements `CredentialInputUpdater` for the recovery-codes type (`RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider` implements only `CredentialProvider` and `CredentialInputValidator`). `updateCredential` therefore returns false and `createCredential` runs as before.
- **Imports and ordering.** The new imports resolve within existing module dependencies, and the tamper check and logout ordering in `RecoveryAuthnCodesAction.processAction` are unchanged.
